name: Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS)
directions: Clinician-rated using the patient report and clinical observations over the previous 48 hours. Use the authorized item anchors. Items 5, 6, 8 and 9 are rated 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; other items are rated 0–4. This is a severity measure, not a diagnosis.

questions.definition: 0 absent; 1 mild or possible increase on questioning; 2 definite subjective elevation; 3 elevated and inappropriate to content; 4 euphoric, inappropriate laughter or singing.
0 absent; 1 subjective increase; 2 animated, increased gestures; 3 excessive energy/hyperactivity, restless but can be calmed; 4 continuous motor excitement, cannot be calmed.
0 normal; 1 mild or possible increase; 2 definite subjective increase; 3 spontaneous sexual content or hypersexual self-report; 4 overt sexual acts.
0 no decrease; 1 up to one hour less; 2 more than one hour less; 3 decreased need for sleep; 4 denies need for sleep.

scale.label: 4 — irritable at times in interview; recent anger/annoyance
4 — increased rate or amount at times

questions.definition: 0 absent; 1 circumstantial, mildly distractible or quick thoughts; 2 distractible, loses goal, frequent topic changes or racing thoughts; 3 flight of ideas, tangential or difficult to follow; 4 incoherent, communication impossible.

scale.label: 6 — grandiose/paranoid ideas or ideas of reference
2 — sarcastic, loud at times or guarded
6 — threatens interviewer, shouting or interview difficult

questions.definition: 0 appropriate dress/grooming; 1 minimally unkempt; 2 poorly groomed, moderately dishevelled or overdressed; 3 dishevelled, partly clothed or garish make-up; 4 completely unkempt or bizarre garb.
0 admits illness and need for treatment; 1 possibly ill; 2 admits behaviour change but denies illness; 3 admits possible behaviour change but denies illness; 4 denies behaviour change.

attribution: Young RC, Biggs JT, Ziegler VE, Meyer DA. A rating scale for mania: reliability, validity and sensitivity. Br J Psychiatry. 1978;133:429–435.
